Their recycling example for "perusahaan Ali" reads "Fair value of portofilio : $34.000 / Less cost of portofolio : $34.000 / Unrealized gain : $4.000"; the cost must be 30,000. Their Saratoga sale states a price of "$95.000.000" but debits cash of $98,500,000, and its entry ("Cash $98.500.000 / Debt Investment $98.185.648,32 / Gain on sale of debt investment $314.351,68") removes only the amortised cost, leaving both the fair value adjustment and the unrealised holding gain on the books. Under PSAK 109 the asset leaves at fair value and the gain is reclassified at the sale, as in the last journal above. And their FVOCI impairment example follows an incurred-loss model; under PSAK 109 the expected credit loss on FVOCI debt is charged to profit with the other side in OCI, so the asset stays at fair value (para. 5.5.2).
edits.replace: By contrast, a sale entry that reads "Cash 98,500,000 / Debt investment 98,185,648.32 / Gain on sale of debt investment 314,351.68" removes only the amortised cost, leaving both the fair value adjustment and the unrealised holding gain on the books. Under PSAK 109 the asset leaves at fair value and the gain is reclassified at the sale, as in the last journal above. Impairment of FVOCI debt follows the expected credit loss model, not an incurred-loss model: the expected credit loss is charged to profit with the other side in OCI, so the asset stays at fair value (para. 5.5.2).
